title: Can't un-set CanvasLayer's custom_viewport property
body:
### Tested versions

encountered in Godot v4.6.3.stable.mono using C#
relevant code looks unchanged in latest

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 5700 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21043.5001) - AMD Ryzen 7 3800XT 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

The custom_viewport property on a CanvasLayer lets you tell that layer to render on a different viewport than the default. Once you set this property to a value, it can't be "cleared".

Per the documentation:
> The custom Viewport node assigned to the CanvasLayer. If null, uses the default viewport instead.

Setting the value to null should use the default viewport, but if you try to set the value to null you get an error: `Cannot set viewport to nullptr.`

This error seems to come from [this line](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ccb8004960b1638f5532048db6c33a0bf5f0769e/scene/main/canvas_layer.cpp#L229), which seems to reject non-null viewports. It seems to me like this is an erroneous check, the fix may even be as simple as deleting that single line.

### Steps to reproduce

set any CanvasLayer's custom_viewport property to some other SubViewport, then try to set it back to default by assigning `custom_viewport = null`
